attachments.origin_landmark: external surfaces of ribs 5-12 (interdigitating with serratus anterior and latissimus dorsi)
attachments.insertion_landmark: iliac crest (anterior half of the outer lip), inguinal ligament, and linea alba via the aponeurosis

actions: laterally flexes and contralaterally rotates trunk (unilateral)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Fibers run obliquely inferomedially ('hands in pockets' direction) -- the most superficial of the three flat abdominal wall layers, and the layer whose fiber direction most differs from transversus abdominis's purely transverse fibers deep to it.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse, in the mid-axillary line between the costal margin and the iliac crest -- the classic transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block window.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Most superficial of the three flat lateral wall muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Three parallel hyperechoic fascial layers over muscle bellies that thin from posterolateral to anterior; fibers run inferomedially ('hands in pockets' direction).
structures_at_risk: intercostal/subcostal neurovascular bundle between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis, one layer deep
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Injected as part of the same lateral-wall preoperative botulinum toxin protocol as internal oblique and transversus abdominis (see those entries) before complex ventral hernia repair.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Quevedo-Cruz D et al., Hernia 30:75 (2026), doi:10.1007/s10029-025-03558-7 -- ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin prehabilitation technique for complex ventral hernia (PubMed); Zamkowski M et al., Pol Przegl Chir 97(6):1 (2025), doi:10.5604/01.3001.0055.3078 -- volumetric muscle elongation by layer after lateral wall injection (PubMed)

trigger_points.location_description: Trigger points scattered through the external oblique, including points below and lateral to the xiphoid process and points lower in the muscle near the inguinal region.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A diffuse local ache through the abdominal wall; points near the costal margin/xiphoid can refer pain to the lower chest and upper abdomen in a pattern that mimics heartburn (with associated nausea or belching), while lower/inguinal points refer pain into the groin and, in men, the testicle.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Chronic coughing, abdominal surgery, and direct strain from twisting/reaching movements.
trigger_points.notes: External oblique trigger points reproducing suprapubic, testicular and groin pain have been documented directly in men with chronic pelvic pain syndrome, not only inferred from the classic Trigger Point Manual chapter.
trigger_points.source: Anderson RU, Sawyer T, Wise D, Morey A, Nathanson BH (2009) "Painful myofascial trigger points and pain sites in men with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome." J Urol 182(6):2753-2758, doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.08.033, PMID 19837420 (PubMed) -- external oblique palpation reproduced suprapubic, testicular and groin pain in at least 80% of patients at those respective pain sites (p<0.01); epigastric/heartburn-mimicking pattern per Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (2nd ed. 1999, Vol 1) external oblique chapter, as reflected in secondary clinical compilations (Niel Asher Education external oblique trigger point reference).

trigger_points.location_description: Trigger points in the external oblique identified by palpation during clinical evaluation of chronic abdominal wall pain.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Localized abdominal wall pain and tenderness that can be mistaken for a hernia, dysmenorrhea, or other intra-abdominal pathology; dry needling of the identified points has produced sustained pain relief.
trigger_points.notes: One of several abdominal wall muscles (with rectus abdominis) implicated in chronic abdominal wall pain of otherwise uncertain origin.
trigger_points.source: Rajkannan P, Vijayaraghavan R (2018) "Dry needling in chronic abdominal wall pain of uncertain origin." J Bodyw Mov Ther 23(1):94-98, doi:10.1016/j.jbmt.2018.01.004, PMID 30691770 (PubMed); Temel MH, Bagcier F (2023) "Abdominal Wall Pain and Primary Dysmenorrhea: The Importance of Myofascial Trigger Points." Complement Med Res 30(4):360-361, doi:10.1159/000530035, PMID 36893743 (PubMed).
